summary: Deep primary-source verification of drone part materials: teardowns, FCC internal photos, RCS papers

result.drone: DJI Mavic 4 Pro (aircraft model L3AB2410, FCC ID SS3-L3AB2410; released May 2025; 1063 g takeoff weight)
confirmed: Propellers: 'Enhanced Nylon Composite Material', model 1158F, 26.7x14.7 cm — stated on DJI official support page (Aircraft Propeller Materials, Dimensions, and Models). PRIMARY/manufacturer CONFIRMED.

Battery: 4S LiPo, Lithium Nickel Manganese Cobalt Oxide (Li-NMC) chemistry, 6654 mAh / 95.3 Wh, 332 g, 14.32 V nominal — DJI Intelligent Flight Battery spec (repair.dji.com). PRIMARY/manufacturer CONFIRMED for chemistry/type. Battery = 332 g of 1063 g = single densest mass in airframe.

FCC certification: model L3AB2410 = Mavic 4 Pro, FCC ID SS3-L3AB2410, granted 2025 with External + Internal Photos on file at fccid.io (Internal Photos 1&2 of 2, dated 2025-06-02). PRIMARY document exists (image OCR not machine-readable in this pass, but filing confirmed).

Overall RCS class (family, not this exact model): measured DJI Mavic Pro mean RCS -8.1 to -19.1 dBsm at 24 GHz; DJI P4 Pro -15.0/-12.4 dBsm at 15/25 GHz (arXiv 1911.05926) — small consumer drones fall roughly -10 to -25 dBsm at mmWave. PRIMARY measurement papers.
conventional: Body/central chassis: SECONDARY consensus = magnesium-alloy internal frame inside a polycarbonate outer shell (multiple reviews: mydeardrone, digitalcameraworld, engadget). One repair source (reboot-hub) instead calls the central chassis 'carbon-fiber-reinforced polyamide'. Conflicting secondary; NOT confirmed by a primary teardown material statement.
Arms: 'high-strength composite' / glass- or carbon-fiber-reinforced polyamide (reboot-hub repair guide, secondary). Arms double as folding landing structure. Convention.

Motors: brushless DC outrunner — copper windings, NdFeB (neodymium) permanent magnets, electrical-steel stator laminations, aluminum/steel bell housing. No DJI/teardown material statement found; universal for this motor class. CONVENTION.

PCB: FR-4 glass-epoxy laminate with copper traces + metal (nickel-silver/steel) RF shielding cans over the SDR/WLAN/BLE RF section. FCC filing confirms multi-band RF PCBs exist; specific shield metal inferred by convention.

Gimbal: magnesium-alloy 3-axis frame (reboot-hub repair guide + gimbal-repair sources, secondary/consistent) with plastic camera housing and small coreless/BLDC gimbal motors (copper + magnets). Frame material semi-corroborated but not primary-confirmed.
Landing gear: no separate landing legs — folded front arms/props serve as ground contact; feet are molded plastic (convention).
Battery casing detail: hard plastic (PC/ABS) outer shell over aluminum-laminate pouch cells (convention; DJI states chemistry, not casing material).

part_materials.motors: Brushless DC: copper windings + NdFeB magnets + electrical-steel laminations + aluminum bell (convention)
part_materials.props: Enhanced Nylon Composite Material, model 1158F (confirmed, DJI official)
part_materials.battery: 4S LiPo Li-NMC pouch cells, 95.3 Wh, 332 g; aluminum-laminate pouches in plastic case (chemistry confirmed DJI; casing convention)
part_materials.gimbal: Magnesium-alloy 3-axis frame + plastic camera housing + coreless gimbal motors (convention/secondary)
part_materials.pcb: FR-4 glass-epoxy + copper + metal RF shielding cans (convention; RF PCB existence confirmed by FCC filing)
part_materials.gear: No dedicated landing gear; folded arms/molded plastic feet act as ground contact (convention)

result.rcs_dominant_metal: "No Mavic-4-Pro-specific component-level dBsm breakdown exists in the literature. Best-supported inference: the dominant metallic scatterers are (1) the 4 brushless motors (metal — copper/steel/magnet mass; measured stronger motor return under HH-pol) and (2) the central LiPo battery pack (largest dense conductive mass, 332 g of aluminum-laminate cells; in the F450 study the battery is the largest reflective object). Airframe body/arms/props are deliberately low-reflectivity nylon/composite (arXiv 1911.05926: 'body frames and propellers made of low-reflective materials like carbon fiber and plastic'). Ranking for this model: battery pack ≈ motors > gimbal-camera metal / RF-shield cans > (props/body negligible). Whole-drone Mavic-class RCS anchor: -8 to -19 dBsm @24 GHz."

result.drone: DJI Matrice 4E / Mavic 3 Enterprise (shared Mavic-3-class platform). Matrice 4 series FCC ID SS3-PM4101703; takeoff weight ~1219 g; standard prop model 1157F (10.8 in). Mavic 3 series prop 9453F.
confirmed: Propellers: DJI official support doc explicitly lists Mavic 3 Series (9453F) as 'Nylon + Rubber' and Matrice 4D/4TD (1364) as 'Composite material' — i.e. glass-fiber/nylon composite, NOT carbon fiber (carbon is reserved for M600/Agras) [CONFIRMED, DJI]
Matrice 4 series standard propeller = 1157F, 10.8 in; takeoff weight 1219 g (standard) / 1229 g (low-noise) [CONFIRMED, DJI specs]

DJI uses magnesium-alloy AZ91 for structural brackets/housings on its Mavic-line drones as documented practice: DJI Inspire 2 'has an AZ91 housing', DJI Mavic Air 'applies brackets based on AZ91', Phantom 4 Pro V2.0 uses a titanium-magnesium hybrid structure [CONFIRMED for those models, peer-reviewed Frontiers review]
Whole-drone RCS is very low because DJI body frames/propellers are low-reflective plastic/nylon composite, per compact-range measurements [CONFIRMED, arXiv 1911.05926]
Measured whole-drone RCS anchors: DJI Phantom 4 Pro -15.03 dBsm @15GHz / -12.40 @25GHz; Inspire 1 -14.24 / -11.09; Mavic Pro -17.06 / -16.20 dBsm (VV) [CONFIRMED, arXiv 1911.05926]
conventional: Body outer shell: high-strength composite plastic (PC/ABS-PC blend). Aggregator specs call Mavic 3 Classic 'high-strength composite plastics and magnesium alloy', but no M4E/Mavic-3-Enterprise-specific teardown confirms the exact polymer [convention]

Internal structural frame/brackets: magnesium alloy (AZ91-class Mg-Al-Zn) — strongly implied by DJI's documented Inspire2/Mavic Air AZ91 practice, but NOT primary-confirmed for the Mavic 3 / Matrice 4E specifically [convention]
Arms: glass-fiber-reinforced polymer / plastic composite housing internal wiring [convention]
Motors: brushless — copper windings, steel shaft, aluminum bell+stator, NdFeB (neodymium) magnets [convention, universal to this motor class]
Battery: Li-ion/Li-Po smart pack — pouch cells with aluminum & copper foil current collectors, graphite/NMC chemistry, in a plastic housing [convention]
Gimbal: aluminum-alloy frame + micro brushless motors + plastic covers [convention]
PCB: FR-4 fiberglass, copper traces, plus stamped-metal EMI shielding cans [convention, universal]
Landing gear: no dedicated gear — folding front-arm tips / small plastic feet serve as landing supports [convention]

result.rcs_dominant_metal: Li-Po/Li-ion BATTERY PACK is the single largest reflective object in small DJI quads — RCS literature reports the DJI F450's RCS closely tracks that of its bare Li-Po battery (battery = dominant scatterer). Secondary metal scatterers: the four motors (copper/steel/aluminum, also the micro-Doppler source), the camera/gimbal metal assembly, and internal PCB EMI shielding. No Matrice-4E/Mavic-3-Enterprise-specific per-part RCS decomposition is published; the plastic/nylon shell and props contribute little (low-reflective). Anchor whole-drone values: Phantom 4 Pro -15.03 dBsm @15GHz / -12.40 @25GHz.

result.drone: DJI Mini 4 Pro (FCC ID SS3-MT4MFVD23) 및 DJI Mini 5 Pro (sub-250g급). 두 기종은 프로펠러 재질이 동일(DJI 공식)하고 구조/재질 계열이 사실상 같음.
confirmed: 프로펠러: Nylon + Rubber(끝단 오렌지 팁) — DJI 공식 'Aircraft Propeller Materials' 지원문서에 Mini 4 Pro와 Mini 5 Pro 모두 'Nylon + Rubber'로 명시 (제조사 1차, 3형). Mini 3 계열은 'Nylon + Glass fiber'로 다름
모터: NdFeB(네오디뮴-철-붕소) 영구자석 + 구리(Cu) 권선 + 규소강(silicon-steel) 적층 스테이터 — DJI 공식 'Inside a Drone: Brushless Motors' 문서에서 DJI 모터 구성으로 명시(제조사 1차, 3형). Mini 전용 도면은 아니나 DJI 브러시리스 모터 공통 구성
배터리: 리튬이온(Li-ion) 화학, 7.32V 공칭(2S), 2590mAh, 18.96Wh — DJI/판매처 사양표 명시(제조사 사양, 3/5형). Mini 4 Pro Intelligent Flight Battery BWX140-2590-7.32
동체 상부/하부 셸: 플라스틱(폴리머) — OEM 교체부품 'Original Upper Shell/Body Cover for Mini 4 Pro'가 전부 플라스틱 성형품(5형 OEM 교체부품). 마그네슘합금 아님(마그네슘은 Mavic 3 프레임)
conventional: 동체 셸/암의 정확한 폴리머 등급(PC/ABS/PA-GF 등)은 teardown이나 FCC 자료에 명시 없음 — 소형 드론 관례상 유리섬유강화 PC/PA(나일론) 계열로 추정. 249g 미달 목표상 경량 플라스틱
암(arm): 동체와 일체형 플라스틱 성형(별도 금속 암 없음) — 관례/구조 추정
짐벌 롤암 브래킷: 알루미늄합금(CNC/양극산화) 소형 금속 브래킷 + FPC + 고무 댐퍼 — 애프터마켓/OEM류 교체부품 설명이 aluminum alloy로 기술(부분 1차, 원부품 등급 미확정 → 관례)
배터리 셀 물리구조: 파우치형 알루미늄-라미네이트 포일 외피 + Cu/Al 집전체, 외부 플라스틱 배터리 하우징 — Li-ion 파우치 셀 관례
PCB/메인보드: FR4 유리섬유 기판 + 구리 배선 + EMI 실드캔(니켈실버/스틸) — FCC 내부사진 PDF를 이미지라 판독 못함, 전자기판 관례 추정
착륙장치: Mini 계열은 별도 랜딩기어 없음 — 암/동체 하부의 소형 플라스틱 발 일체형(관례)

part_materials.motors: NdFeB 네오디뮴 자석 + 구리 권선 + 규소강 적층 스테이터, 4개 (confirmed, DJI 공식 모터 구성)

part_materials.gimbal: 알루미늄합금 롤암 브래킷 + FPC + 고무 댐퍼 (부분 confirmed / 원부품 등급 convention)
part_materials.gear: 별도 랜딩기어 없음; 플라스틱 일체형 발 (convention)

result.rcs_dominant_metal: 부품별 분해 RCS(component-level decomposition) 측정 논문은 찾지 못함 — 확인된 소형드론 RCS 논문(compact-range 1911.05926)은 기체 전체 평균값만 보고(DJI Phantom4Pro -15.03dBsm@15GHz, -12.40dBsm@25GHz; Inspire1Pro 유사), 배터리/모터/PCB 기여를 분리하지 않음. 따라서 지배 금속은 '측정 인용'이 아니라 물리 추론: (1) 배터리 팩 = 단일 최대 연속 도전성 질량 → 정적/코히어런트 반사 지배 추정, (2) 4× 모터(네오디뮴+규소강, 조밀 금속) = 마이크로도플러 및 회전 반사 지배, (3) 카메라/짐벌 금속 브래킷 + PCB 실드캔 = 부차. 정직한 결론: Mini급의 부품별 dBsm 실측 근거는 없음, 지배 후보는 배터리·모터(공동 지배)이며 이는 미확정 추론.

result.drone: DJI Phantom 4 Pro V2.0 (model WM331, FCC ID SS3-WM331S1801)
confirmed: Gimbal + camera housing = magnesium alloy + ceramics — stated verbatim on DJI official support/FAQ page ('it is made of a magnesium alloy and ceramics')

Internal load-bearing core/gimbal housing is a magnesium alloy (~90% Mg / 9% Al / 1% Zn, i.e. AZ91-type) — confirmed by hands-on teardown (droneflyers 'Under the Hood', boards screw into a magnesium core)
Airframe uses titanium-alloy + magnesium-alloy structural construction 'to increase rigidity and reduce weight' — DJI official marketing/spec copy (Phantom 4 Pro / P4P V2.0)
Outer fuselage shell is plastic (ABS-type); iFixit repair guide refers to it as the 'plastic shell' and droneflyers contrasts the Mg core against the ABS-plastic body
Landing gear / legs are plastic — droneflyers teardown ('plastic access hatches', plastic legs)
Propellers (9455S low-noise, quick-release) are plastic — DJI/OEM parts spec ('top-grade plastic', 11.7 g each, 9.4 in)
Intelligent Flight Battery is a 4S Li-polymer pack, 15.2 V / 5870 mAh / 89.2 Wh, in a plastic case — DJI spec

RCS measurements of the DJI Phantom / small consumer quadcopters show the non-plastic parts (battery pack + motors, plus copper wiring) dominate the radar return; plastic shell/props contribute little (Li & Ling UT-Austin ISAR; Phantom 2 FEM-MoM paper)
conventional: Propeller exact polymer = polycarbonate/glass-filled nylon — only 'plastic' is confirmed by sources; specific resin is industry-convention assumption, not stated by DJI

Brushless motor internals: copper stator windings + NdFeB permanent magnets + aluminum-alloy bell/rotor and steel shaft — standard BLDC construction; one third-party OEM replacement lists an 'aluminum alloy' motor joint, but DJI does not publish the OEM motor material

Main flight-controller/ESC PCB = FR-4 substrate with copper traces and tin-plated steel/copper RF shielding cans — standard practice; FCC internal-photo PDFs exist (SS3-WM331S1801) but images were not machine-readable to confirm directly
Battery cell internals: aluminum + copper current-collector foils inside the LiPo pouches — inherent to Li-polymer chemistry (convention, not separately documented for this pack)
Arms are non-removable and formed as part of the plastic upper/lower shell (fixed-arm Phantom design) — inferred from teardown geometry, not an explicit DJI material statement

part_materials.body: Plastic outer shell (ABS-type) over an internal magnesium-alloy core; airframe reinforced with titanium+magnesium alloy (confirmed)
part_materials.arms: Plastic, integral with the fixed shell (fixed-arm design) (convention/teardown-inferred)
part_materials.motors: Brushless: copper windings + NdFeB magnets + aluminum-alloy bell + steel shaft (convention; 3rd-party OEM notes aluminum-alloy)
part_materials.battery: 4S Li-polymer pouch cells, 15.2V/5870mAh, plastic case, Al/Cu internal foils (LiPo+case=confirmed; foils=convention)
part_materials.pcb: FR-4 with copper traces + metal RF shielding cans (convention)

result.rcs_dominant_metal: Battery pack (Li-polymer) is the single largest / dominant scatterer, with the four brushless motors second; copper battery-to-ESC wiring also contributes. In HH-polarization motor returns can exceed the battery. Measured on small DJI/consumer quads at X-band ~10 GHz: peak RCS roughly -9 to -14 dBsm (mean ~0.01 m^2 / -20 dBsm), with plastic shell/props contributing negligibly. Sources: Li & Ling ISAR (peaks -3 to -27.5 dBsm, 'non-plastic portions dominate — motors, battery pack'); Schröder et al. DJI Phantom 2 FEM-MoM at 10 GHz (metallic scatterers = battery + engines + copper cables, plastic hull nearly transparent). NOTE: these are Phantom-2/generic small-quad measurements, not a Phantom 4 Pro V2-specific measurement.

result.drone: DJI Spreading Wings S1000+ (octocopter, 8 arms, 4114 pro motors, 1552 folding props, ~4.4kg empty / 11kg MTOW)
confirmed: Frame arms: carbon fiber — stated verbatim on DJI official feature page ('All frame arms ... are made from carbon fiber')
Retractable landing gear: carbon fiber — DJI official feature page ('the retractable landing gear are made from carbon fiber')
OEM 1552 folding propeller: 'High strength performance engineered plastics' — DJI official S1000 spec page (NOT carbon fiber for the DJI-brand prop)
Each arm integrates a 40A ESC and a 4114 pro brushless motor; per-arm assembly (arm+motor+ESC+prop) ~325 g — DJI official
conventional: Center frame plates: carbon-fiber laminate top/bottom plates with aluminum standoffs/support pillars and aluminum arm-mount clamps — DJI does not quote the plate material on the pages checked; inferred from spare-parts (Part 09 'Center Frame Support Pillar', arm-mount hardware) and standard S-series construction

Motor 4114 internals: aluminum-alloy bell/housing, copper stator windings, sintered NdFeB permanent magnets, silicon-steel stator laminations — standard brushless-outrunner construction; DJI does not publish per-material breakdown
Battery: 6S LiPo (~10-20 Ah), aluminum-laminate soft pouch cells with Cu/Al foil electrodes and Ni/Cu tabs — battery not included in S1000+ kit; user-supplied, so material is generic LiPo convention
Gimbal (Zenmuse Z15 series, sold separately): CNC-machined aluminum-alloy structure — not officially quoted for Z15; inferred from DJI camera-gimbal practice
ESC / PCB / power-distribution board: FR4 fiberglass substrate with copper traces and planes — universal PCB convention, not DJI-stated
Third-party 1552 replacement props are often carbon-fiber/nylon composite; only the DJI OEM prop is confirmed engineered plastic

part_materials.body: center frame: carbon-fiber laminate plates + aluminum standoffs/arm-mount clamps (convention; arms-CF confirmed, plate material inferred)
part_materials.motors: aluminum bell + copper windings + NdFeB magnets + silicon-steel laminations (convention)
part_materials.props: DJI OEM 1552: high-strength engineered plastic (confirmed - DJI spec); 3rd-party variants carbon/nylon (convention)
part_materials.battery: LiPo aluminum-laminate pouch, Cu/Al foils (convention; not in kit, user-supplied)
part_materials.gimbal: Zenmuse Z15 CNC aluminum alloy (convention; sold separately)
part_materials.pcb: FR4 fiberglass + copper (ESC 40A and power board) (convention)
part_materials.gear: carbon fiber retractable landing gear (confirmed - DJI official)

result.rcs_dominant_metal: Motors are the dominant metallic scatterers. Small-drone RCS measurement literature reports that in HH polarization the motors give the strongest returns while the battery gives weaker returns (Li & Ling, 'Radar Signatures of Small Consumer Drones', UT-Austin; compact-range measurements at 15/25 GHz, arXiv:1911.05926). Overall small-quadcopter body RCS is low (~ -17 dBsm HH at X-band with up to 15 dB frequency trenches) precisely because the airframe is low-reflectivity plastic/carbon-fiber, leaving the metallic motor cluster (Cu windings + steel laminations + Al bell, ×8 on the S1000+) as the primary bright points; carbon fiber itself is conductive and contributes secondary edge/plate returns. No S1000-specific per-part dBsm teardown paper was found.
